title: Jacob Misiorowski breaks his velocity record in one-hit shutout with 15 Ks
content:
With Milwaukee Brewers flamethrower Jacob Misiorowski starting Friday night’s series opener against the Philadelphia Phillies, and Phillies ace Cristopher Sánchez scheduled to pitch Sunday, Misiorowski had a chance to set the tone for a highly anticipated series featuring this season’s most dominant starting pitchers.

He wasted no time, striking out leadoff man Kyle Schwarber with a 104.5 mph four-seamer that set a record for velocity from a starting pitcher since MLB tracking began in 2008 — breaking the record he set when he threw a pitch 103.7 mph in his last start, in Denver against the Colorado Rockies.

But that was just the beginning of one of the most brilliant outings in recent memory. The man known as “Miz” pitched a one-hit shutout while striking out 15 in just 95 pitches in Milwaukee’s 6-0 win. It was the most strikeouts in a game known as a “Maddux,” breaking Tarik Skubal’s previous record of 13. Named for Hall of Famer Greg Maddux, a “Maddux” is a complete-game shutout with under 100 pitches thrown.

Misiorowski blew past his career-high for innings, which was seven before Friday’s masterful performance. He’s thrown more than 95 pitches five times in his career, with his highest pitch count (108) coming in a seven-inning outing against the Pittsburgh Pirates on Sept. 7, 2025. He also crushed his former high for strikeouts in a game, which was 12 (May 25 against the St. Louis Cardinals, and July 8, 2025, against the Los Angeles Dodgers).

The 24-year-old righty actually set another (short-lived) velocity record earlier in the matchup with Schwarber. After falling behind with two balls that both registered 103.4 mph, Misiorowski threw a 104.0 mph fastball for a strike. Two pitches later, Schwarber argued with home-plate umpire Chad Fairchild after striking out on a foul tip against the record-breaking pitch.

Misiorowski continued his remarkable first inning by striking out Trea Turner on a 103.5 mph pitch. Then came a three-pitch strikeout of Bryce Harper, where Misiorowski sandwiched a 90.7 mph curveball with two fastballs that registered 104.1 and 104.2 mph.

Sánchez actually leads major-league pitchers in fWAR with 3.9. Still, Misiorowski entered Friday’s action with a 3.2 fWAR and commanding lead among qualified pitchers in strikeout rate (13.4 strikeouts per nine innings, with Sánchez second at 10.9). He also has the best ERA among starters at 1.34, ahead of Sánchez (1.54).

Schwarber did enact some revenge in his next at-bat with the only hit the Phillies could muster all night: a single on a 90.8 mph slider to lead off the fourth inning after Misiorowski struck out eight of the first nine hitters he faced. Then Misiorowski struck out Turner again before getting Harper to ground into a double play to end the inning.

Before facing the Phillies, Misiorowski was responsible for 28 of the 30 recorded pitches thrown 103-plus mph by starting pitchers since tracking began, and all 28 of those came this season.
